speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia and a significant medical history; to begin our assessment, how long have you been experiencing these coordination difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the right-sided predominance is a key detail. Have you noticed any weakness or numbness on that side, or have you experienced any falls yet?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST TEST: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for oligoclonal bands and JC virus PCR.
Your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab for a year significantly raises the concern for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML); have you noticed any changes in your vision or speech along with your coordination issues?

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: MRI Brain: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. CSF Oligoclonal bands: Negative. CSF JC virus PCR: Positive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, combined with a positive JC virus PCR in your cerebrospinal fluid, confirm this diagnosis. Given your history of natalizumab use for Crohn's disease, this is a known serious adverse reaction.
